content.purpose: Collapse repeated records and count how often each one occurs.
content.mentalModel: uniq only compares adjacent lines, so unsorted input must usually pass through sort first. -c prefixes each group with its count.

demonstration.explanation: This small example isolates the main idea behind removing duplicates.

remember: uniq only compares adjacent lines, so unsorted input must usually pass through sort first. -c prefixes each group with its count.
Verify the resulting state before moving on.

tasks.instruction: Count each unique service name and save “3 api”, “1 db”, “2 web” as sorted lines in /home/student/answers/service-counts.txt.
hints: Repeated names are not adjacent in the source.
awk can normalise the leading spaces in the count output.
alternateSolutions: awk '{count[$0]++} END {for (name in count) print count[name], name}' /home/student/lab/services.txt | sort -k2 > /home/student/answers/service-counts.txt
